Ava: Pushed a canary enabling FP8 (transformer engine) on the H100 pool this morning. Seeing 15-25% tail latency regression on long sequences (>=1024). Not sure if kernel selector is flipping to a slower fallback or if KV cache interactions are blowing up. Repro below, attaching quick profiler output.

Ravi: Can you paste the profiler p50/p95/p99 and the kernel selection log? Also what TE fp8 mode and kernel_selector did you use? seq len / batch size? @Liu FYI in case it's a kernel-level issue.

Ava: Profiler snippet:
```
model: gpt-xxl
config: TE_FP8=1; TE_FP8_MODE=dynamic; KERNEL_SELECTOR=auto
workload: seq=2048, batch=1, kv_cache=enabled
p50: 82ms, p95: 260ms, p99: 540ms
hot kernels:
 - te_attention_fp8 (launchs: 420) avg: 0.8ms
 - matmul_fp8_fallback (launchs: 120) avg: 3.4ms
 - kv_cache_commit (launchs: 1) avg: 12ms
notes: spikes align with cache flushes / kernel switches
```

Liu: That matmul_fp8_fallback line is suspicious — on H100 TE sometimes falls back to a slower INT8/FP16 path when scaling/amax calibration is out of range or when KV cache causes unusual tiled sizes. On L40S we saw different behavior: FP8 kernels were consistently chosen but with small-batch inefficiencies.

Liu: Quick checklist to isolate:
 - force KERNEL_SELECTOR=prefer_fp8 (see if fallback vanishes)
 - try batch=4 and continuous batching (min_batch_size=2) to amortize kernel overhead
 - repro w/ kv_cache disabled to see if cache commit/rewrites are the culprit

Maya: Also consider calibration noise: dynamic FP8 modes rely on streaming amax statistics. If a short canary had extreme tokens, the amax window can bias the kernel choice. Re-run calibration with longer warmup (eg. TE_FP8_CALIB_WARMUP=1000) and use bias_correction=1. We saw 10-12% tail help for long sequences.

Ravi: Can you try a config override for kernel selector and post the TE kernel log? Command to reproduce locally (python but same env):
```
TE_FP8=1 TE_FP8_MODE=dynamic KERNEL_SELECTOR=prefer_fp8 python -m redwood.infer.run \ 
 --model gpt-xxl --seq_len 2048 --batch 1 --kv_cache
```
Also run `export TE_LOG=kernel_selection,launch` before starting to capture which kernel variant is chosen per op.

perf-bot: perf/canary-fp8-h100/1772567890 completed :warning: p99 regressed +18% vs baseline. Dashboard: https://perf.internal/runs/1772567890

Ava: Thanks — will try prefer_fp8 + longer calib and a batch=4 run. If that narrows to KV cache commits, I can instrument commit path. Opening issue: #INFR-1289 with logs and profiler.

Liu: If prefer_fp8 hides it, still check quality — sometimes prefer_fp8 forces a kernel that is faster but produces slightly different quant rounding; run eval set quick check. If quality is fine, we can opt kernel pin for h100 and keep auto on L40S.

Maya: One more gotcha: transformer engine driver had a small allocator regression that amplified launch latency when many kernel types are used in a single request. If you see many unique kernel names per request, that's a hint. We had a fix in te-driver v0.9.3 — confirm te-driver version on the canary.

Ava: Good call — canary uses te-driver 0.9.2. I'll upgrade to 0.9.3 in the canary next run and try the other knobs. Will report back with numbers and kernel logs. :thumbsup:
